Ben — quick legal take:
- Baseline: prefer 'fees paid during the relevant 12-month period' when offering an annual reset. It's easier to calculate and aligns risk to consumption.
- Multiplier: 2x annual fees is reasonable for commercial customers but we should preserve the right to cap certain carve-outs (IP indemnity, gross negligence/data breach) differently.
- Aggregate vs annual: aggregate cap (total across term) is safest for Redwood financially on long-term multi-year deals; annual reset can be granted as a concession tied to either a higher multiplier or a minimum revenue commitment.

Suggested fallback language for order form (two bullets to test with Novus):
1) Annual reset option: "Customer's liability for damages shall be limited to the greater of (i) $250,000 or (ii) two times the fees paid by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim."
2) Aggregate option: "Customer's liability for damages shall be limited to the greater of (i) $750,000 or (ii) the total fees paid under the Order Form during the Term."

Carve-outs: always carve out IP indemnity, willful misconduct and obligations under data protection laws (we can agree to reasonable actions for breach but not unlimited exposure).

I'll draft redline language and an amendment that offers annual reset for the first two years if they commit to a 36-month term.

—Laura

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@novushealth.com>, Novus Health Legal <legal@novushealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-19 08:22 PDT
Subject: Proposed compromise on cap mechanics (attached)

Sara — thanks for the redline. Per internal review we've put together two compromise options (attached XLS + amendment):

Option A — Annual-reset (Novus preferred):
- Liability limited to the greater of (i) $300,000 or (ii) two times the fees paid in the prior 12-month period.
- Applies on a rolling 12-month basis with an annual reconciliation at each anniversary.
- Carve-outs: IP indemnity, gross negligence/willful misconduct, and obligations under applicable data protection laws (e.g., regulatory fines) are excluded from the cap.

Option B — Contract-aggregate (Redwood default):
- Liability limited to the greater of (i) $900,000 or (ii) total fees paid under the Order Form for the Term.
- Simpler administratively; provides certainty over multi-year exposure.

We propose Option A for Year 1 with a 36-month Order Form (minimum commit) if Novus will accept a 2.5x multiplier in Year 3 or revert to Option B at renewal. That gives Novus annual alignment and Redwood protection on long tail risk.

Would Novus legal be open to reviewing Option A with the amendment tied to a renewal-triggered multiplier? If so, we'll provide a tracked redline of the Order Form and a short amendment.

Best,
Ben

Ben — thanks, that split of options is helpful. A few follow-ups from our counsel:
1) For Option A, can you add an explicit example calculation in the amendment to avoid disputes (we suggested sample math for a $1.2M ARR customer).
2) We need clarity on whether regulatory penalties (e.g., HIPAA fines) are a carve-out or subject to mitigation; our counsel typically asks that statutory penalties remain outside the cap.
3) Regarding the Year 3 2.5x trigger — can Redwood cap the Year 3 maximum at a set dollar figure rather than an open multiplier? Counsel prefers a hard cap for terminal years.

If Redwood can accept: (i) a small example table, (ii) treating statutory penalties as outside the cap, and (iii) a defined Year 3 cap of $3.5M (instead of open multiplier), we can present to procurement for sign-off.

—Novus Legal
